[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] Markley Group is a privately held data center operator headquartered at One Summer Street in Boston, founded in 1991 by Jeff Markley, who is widely credited with pioneering the carrier hotel concept in the data center industry, and who has said the company is built around long-term investment for clients rather than shareholder returns. Markleys Boston flagship facility spans 920,000 square feet of secured white and mechanical space, launched in 1998, and is marketed as New Englands largest and longest-operating multi-tenant mission-critical telecommunications and data center facility, with the company stating it has never experienced a primary power outage in more than 15 years of operation. The company also operates a 352,000 square foot mission-critical facility in Lowell, Massachusetts, which press coverage from CBS Boston and NBC Boston has described as the largest data center in the state and which has become a focal point of local community friction as Markley pursues AI-driven capacity expansion there, with neighbors quoted referring to the facility as the dungeon. Across its US and European portfolio, Markley reports more than 3 million square feet of data center space, offering colocation, high-density colocation, hybrid cloud, disaster recovery, and infrastructure-as-a-service alongside connectivity and managed services to financial services, healthcare, academic, government, and technology customers. As a long-established, founder-led private operator concentrated in the Boston metro market with recent expansion pressure from AI workloads, Markleys profile in this registry parallels other legacy regional colocation providers now navigating the same AI-driven demand surge affecting national wholesale developers. This research was carried out at the operator level in an earlier phase of this project.
